problem:
Negate the following statement:

$\,$ All prime numbers are not divisible by $5.$
worked_solution:
Let $P$ be the set of prime numbers. The given statement can be re-phrased as follows:

$\,$ For all $x\in P,$ $x$ is not divisible by $5.$

Introducing the universal quantifier, we get the following:

$\,$ $∀x\in P,\,x\text{ is not divisible by }5.$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∀x\in P,\,x\text{ is not divisible by }5.) & ≡∃x\in P,\,¬(x\text{ is not divisible by }5.) \\  & ≡∃x\in P,\,x\text{ is divisible by }5.\end{aligned}
$$

which reads 

$\,$ There exists $x\in P$ such that $x$ is divisible by $5.$

or simply

$\,$ Some prime numbers are divisible by $5.$
